title: Light-touch review notes for small PR + refactor ideas
content:
Quick context:
- Small PR (runtime): reduce locking granularity in kv_cache manager. Author: Ethan. Goal: drop occasional 20ms tail for concurrent get/put.
- Looks safe on surface but touches cache invalidation paths used by streaming.

Checklist (quick, first-pass):
- [ ] Does change preserve existing public API of KV cache? (yes, no signature changes)
- [ ] Any new allocs per-token in hot path? (scan for std::vector/reserve in hot loop)
- [ ] Mutex vs RWLock tradeoffs — are there any cases where we now hold write lock during long op?
- [ ] Tests: unit + integration + streaming smoke? (unit added, integration missing)
- [ ] Perf tests: microbenchmark or CI perf job updated? (none)
- [ ] Logging/metrics: any counter for skipped invalidations or dropped entries? (no)

Notes from code dive (file-level):
- kv_cache.h/.cpp: new sharded-lock KVS looks ok, but ctor takes shard_count param with no validation. Potential OOB when shard_count=0 from config. Add assert or fallback 1.
- streaming_manager.cpp: call site assumes single-shard semantics for invalidatePrefix — now may touch multiple shards; need to confirm ordering/race with in-flight requests.
- tests/kv_cache_test.cpp: added basic concurrent put/get; missing test for invalidatePrefix racing with read-with-kvcache-lookup during streaming continuation.

Refactor ideas (future, not blocking):
- Move shard selection logic into a small utility class so both streaming_manager and kv_cache share deterministic hashing; prevents subtle divergence.
- Introduce a ScopedReadGuard that captures metrics (hold_time_ms) for locks — helps perf debugging later. Could be optional macro compiled in debug/perf builds.
- Consider replacing raw mutexes with folly::SharedMutex if we want clearer read-heavy semantics across platforms. Evaluate kernel-level vs userspace cost on target infra.

Risks / TODOs before merge:
- Add integration test that simulates streaming request where invalidatePrefix happens mid-stream. Repro script below.
- Confirm there is no burst of allocation due to temporary vectors when single-shard -> multi-shard path triggers. Run asan + valgrind on unit tests.
- Verify metrics/observability: add a gauge or counter for shard_migrations/invalidation_ops to track in canary.

Local repro steps (quick):
1) repo: runtime/
2) checkout PR branch; build with DEBUG=1
3) run tests: bazel test //tests:kv_cache_integration_test --config=local
4) repro server: ./bazel-bin/runtime/bin/streaming_repro --concurrent-streams=100 --invalidate-interval-ms=50
5) Observe tail latency p50/p95 via simple log reporter (script in tools/perf/collect_tail.sh)

Questions for author (send as review comment):
- Why shard_count allowed to be zero? Any external config path that might do this? (line 122 in ctor)
- invalidatePrefix now loops shards in numeric order — can that cause a brief period where some shards report "not found" for a key that existed? Should we add a temporary forwarding map to avoid partial invalidations?
- Can we get a microbenchmark of old vs new lock strategy under 8/32/64 concurrent threads? Good to attach numbers to PR.

Follow-ups (post-merge suggestions):
- Add CI perf job that runs lightweight microbenchmark on kv_cache every night and alerts on regressions.
- Add a short design doc (1-pager) describing cache sharding approach and rationale; move refactor items into it. Link: CONFLUENCE TODO.
- Schedule 30m pairing with Ethan to discuss ScopedReadGuard implementation and metricization.

Notes to self:
- If author pushes fix for shard_count validation, re-run integration tests and microbench locally.
- File a quick Jira (INF-1342) to track perf CI item if not already present (linked above).

Estimated impact/priority: medium — likely improves tail latency for read-heavy workloads but introduces risk in streaming invalidation edge cases. Recommend blocking on: integration test + shard_count validation + perf numbers.

Random fragments / brainstorming (keep, may be deleted later):
- Could we use sequence numbers per key to avoid full invalidatePrefix? Instead mark tombstone with seq > N and lazily evict — avoids widespread locking but increases complexity.
- Maybe add fast-path optimistic check: try read with no lock, then fallback to read lock if mismatch. Might reduce contention on very hot keys.

End of scratchpad.
